intended_object: This is the canonical isomorphism F' ≅ G' between two left Kan extensions along the same L, where F' extends F, G' extends G and F ≅ G. It is the uniqueness of left Kan extensions up to unique isomorphism, compatible with the given isomorphism i. The intent comes from the docstring.
explanation:
The forward map is the morphism F' ⟶ G' that the universal property of (F', α) gives for the 2-cell F ≅ G ⟶ L ⋙ G', namely i.hom ≫ β. The inverse is the symmetric construction from (G', β) using i.inv ≫ α. The two maps compose to the identity because of the uniqueness (hom_ext) part of the universal property. This is the standard argument and the standard canonical isomorphism.

The setting is fully general: arbitrary categories, arbitrary L, and Kan extensions expressed through the `IsLeftKanExtension` predicate, with no extra hypotheses. The special case i = refl is `leftKanExtensionUnique`, which is defined just below in terms of this declaration. So this is the general version and is not too narrow. It is a data-valued formulation of a genuine mathematical fact (the canonical comparison isomorphism), and it is stated correctly.
